newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Tajik police kill 20 prisoners during jail riot.
newsitem.headline: Tajik police kill 20 prisoners during jail riot.

text.p: About 20 inmates at a labour camp in northern Tajikistan were killed on Thursday when government security forces stormed the jail to put down a riot, a senior regional official said on Friday.

"After three days of fruitless negotiations with the riot leaders, the authorities were forced to send in police," Olimdzhon Jalolov, a senior official with the northern Leninabad regional administration, told Reuters by telephone. He also said about 30 prisoners and one policeman at the labour camp in the town of Khudjand were injured.

"There were about 20 prisoners killed during the shooting," Jalolov said. He said the prisoners had demanded the release of Ikrom Ashurov, a convicted criminal and the alleged leader of the riot, and 10 other inmates.

"There demands were unacceptable for us, they were criminals, murderers," Jalolov said. An interior ministry source said elite OMON troops had been flown in from the capital Dushanbe to put down the riot, which began on Tuesday.

On Thursday, officials at the former Soviet republic's Interior Ministry said that order had been restored at the camp and that three prison guards taken hostage had been released. Militia sources said Ashurov was killed in the clash.
Tajikistan is a mountainous country bordering Afghanistan and China and is trying to recover from a bitter civil war.
